title: Smart glasses are getting creepy — so HTC just added a kill switch for bystanders
excerpt: Options include prescription ZEISS lenses in multiple styles and a Power Boost accessory with rapid 50 percent charging.
content_html:
Published Sep 3, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT

Sara Heritage is a tech and gaming journalist, who's currently making her way up to Master Ball rank in Pokemon Champions. Bylines in IGN, GAMINGbible, The Gamer and more. You can usually find her tinkering with tech, or restoring old consoles, always with one of her 3 cats nearby. Come and talk with her over on Twitter @SHeritageJourno.

Summary

  • VIVE Eagle is privacy-first: LED alerts, multi-sensor blocking, voice "Stop filming", and no recording when unworn.
  • Hands-free AI: live translation (90+ languages) and meeting notes; use OpenAI or Gemini. Requests deidentified, not used to train.
  • Starts at $499, ships Sept 3 in EU/NA/AU; 12MP 3K stabilized video, ZEISS lenses, 6h use, 50% charge in 10 min.

HTC has just launched the VIVE Eagle, a direct response to the privacy concerns associated with Meta's AI glasses. The new AI-powered smart glasses promise all the hands-free features one would expect—such as AI assistance, POV capture, and live translation—without making you or anyone around you unwitting surveillance subjects.

Here’s what the VIVE Eagle can do

Privacy-first AI smart glasses come with important safeguards

HTC has placed a strong focus on privacy with the VIVE Eagle, incorporating safety measures that guard both the wearer and those nearby—this is a direct reaction to the criticism that Meta has received for not adequately protecting the privacy of people who are not directly involved.

VIVE Eagle takes a privacy-first approach for you and the people around you. When filming or taking a photo, a notification LED illuminates or pulses. The LED even automatically adjusts its brightness in different conditions to ensure it’s always visible. A multi-sensor approach means VIVE Eagle will not film if the notification LED is obscured, damaged or compromised. Similarly, VIVE Eagle cannot record if the glasses are not being worn. What’s more, a setting can be enabled so if people nearby don’t want to be filmed they can say, “Stop filming” and VIVE Eagle will stop recording.

However, these glasses are not solely concerned with privacy; they are also fitted with a sharp 12MP camera that can record 3K video with electronic stabilization, ensuring that your video looks smooth whether you are moving or standing still.

The VIVE AI system provides real-time translation (available in over 90 languages), automatically generates meeting notes, and includes hands-free support, making the glasses useful for travel, work, and daily life. Users can use either the OpenAI or Google Gemini AI models, and each request is de-identified to avoid profiling and isn't used to build data sets on you.

For style-conscious buyers, VIVE Eagle offers premium ZEISS lenses in a variety of options: clear blue light blocking, sun lenses with Category 3 UV400 protection, and photochromic adaptive lenses. Frames are available in both square and pantos shapes, and each comes in multiple colors including black, coffee, berry, navy, and brown.

A major point for me is that there are prescription lens options and fast installation, which make them suitable for everyday use if you're as blind as I am. Disappointingly, there’s no information available on how much this will cost to install in them.

You also won’t need to charge your glasses for ages, prescription or not, since HTC's fast-charging technology lets the battery reach 50% in just 10 minutes, offering up to 6 hours of active use, with an optional Power Boost battery pack for full-day outings.

VIVE Eagle can now be ordered starting at $499 / £429 / €469 and will be available in various styles and colours from 3 September in Europe, North America, and Australia. The optional Power Boost battery accessory costs $49 / £45 / €49. All purchases come with two years of VIVE AI Plus free of charge. VIVE AI Plus provides enhanced AI features, priority customer support, extra storage for photos and videos, and regular updates with the latest capabilities, adding even more value to the glasses.
